primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_t': 'observable state at time t (points)', 'h_t': 'hidden streak state at time t (hot/cold)', 'o_t': 'observation vector at time t (features)', 'P(s_{t+1}|h_t)': 'transition probability (dimensionless)'}

reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies in separating pre-game and in-play models: pre-game picks rely on static probabilistic forecasts, whereas in-game WP models condition on evolving game state. The lock timestamp t_lock acts as a bifurcation point where the model switches from predictive to diagnostic mode. The mathematical structure of in-game WP is best captured by generative score models such as those in 1704.00197, which compute WP as a function of current score differential S(t) and time remaining. These models are not suitable for pre-game use because they assume a known game state. The state machine formalizes this transition, where q_pre_game evolves to q_in_play at t_lock. The Bayesian HMM introduces a hidden layer to model streakiness, allowing dynamic confidence adjustment. This is mathematically expressed as a belief update over hidden states h_t, conditioned on observations o_t and previous states s_t. The failure mode arises when the model assumes stationarity in the underlying process, leading to miscalibration in volatile game segments.
